newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasani retraces some losses after fall.
newsitem.headline: Sasani retraces some losses after fall.

text.p: Shares in media group Sasani Ltd rallied on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Tuesday retracing some recent heavy losses which have stripped more than 30 percent off the stock's value in the past three weeks.
By 1330 GMT Sasani was up nine cents to 96 cents in fairly active trade of almost two million shares.

Dealers said that Sasani's recent fall, which saw it sink to a year low of 79 cents on Monday, may follow talk that the potential selling price of entertainment firm Interleisure Ltd, which Sasani is believed to be keen to buy, may be higher than expected.
"When there was talk that Interleisure might go for 1.2 billion rand, that's around eight rand a share, then there was a lot of interest (in Sasani)," one dealer said.

"But now people are talking of a price closer to 1.5 billion rand or between nine and 10.50 rand a share...This might suit Primedia better," he said, referring to talk that broadcasting and publishing group Primedia Ltd was also keen to buy into Interleisure.
Primedia issued a cautionary announcement on June 17, saying that it was in unspecified talks.
Interleisure shares were last trading at 770 cents, up 10 cents on the day.
Talk that Interleisure is to be sold off comes amid the unbundling of Servgro International which together with Kersaf Ltd jointly own Interleisure.

Kersaf chairman Buddy Hawton told Reuters in May that discussions had been held with a number of parties, including Sasani which has specialist film equipment and post-production video operations and recently bought an advertising firm.
Other dealers said that Sasani's three-week slide may have been prompted by perceptions that it was overpriced following its acquisition in March of the Movie Camera Co Ltd.
"To pay for their last acquisition they issued new shares at 70 cents each. People might have suddenly thought: 'Why am I then paying over 120 cents for Sasani?" one dealer said.
Before its recent slide Sasani was trading as high as 128 cents.
Sasani was not immediately available for comment.
